name: Congenital Portosystemic Shunt

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical features

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of abnormal vascular communication between portal venous system and systemic circulation
Absence or significant reduction of portal vein flow into the liver on Doppler ultrasound or angiography
Presence of clinical manifestations such as hepatic encephalopathy or pulmonary hypertension without other causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of portosystemic shunt with absence or reduction of portal flow into the liver
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver biopsy and genetic testing may assist but are not mandatory for diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Neurocognitive impairment due to shunting of portal blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hepatic nodular lesions (benign regenerative nodules or focal nodular hyperplasia)
pathognomonic.notes: Detected on imaging, characteristic of altered hepatic perfusion

common.notes: Elevated blood ammonia levels due to bypass of hepatic metabolism
Delayed physical development in pediatric patients
Mild to moderate elevation of transaminases and bilirubin

occasional.notes: Hypoxemia due to intrapulmonary vascular dilatations
From varices or portal hypertension complications

searchTerms: confusion and seizures from liver disease

rare.notes: Complication secondary to altered portal flow

rare.symptomName: Cardiac failure secondary to high-output state
rare.notes: Rare complication due to large shunts
searchTerms: heart failure due to high blood flow

imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing absent or reduced portal vein flow
CT or MRI demonstrating portosystemic shunt anatomy
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic
other: Liver biopsy may show nodular regenerative hyperplasia
Pulmonary function tests indicating hypoxemia in hepatopulmonary syndrome

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of portal vein thrombosis or cirrhosis
Elevated portal pressure with preserved portal flow
Absence of congenital vascular shunt on imaging
Usually associated with high-output cardiac failure

redFlags: Rapid onset of hepatic encephalopathy in a child
Severe pulmonary hypertension unexplained by cardiac or lung disease
Progressive liver dysfunction with nodular lesions on imaging
references: Miyamoto et al., Congenital portosystemic shunts: clinical features and management, World J Hepatol, 2020
Orphanet Report Series: Congenital portosystemic shunt, Orphanet, 2023
Franchi-Abella et al., Congenital portosystemic shunts in children: recognition, evaluation, and management, Semin Liver Dis, 2018
